claims.text: The unmodified (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a large caloric response under applied magnetic and pressure fields.
The unmodified alloy has poor mechanical integrity and tends to crack.
Nb is a ductile, high-melting-point element suitable for reinforcing this alloy.
Adding approximately 5 vol% Nb under controlled synthesis conditions will form Nb-rich precipitates in situ along grain boundaries.
Finely dispersed Nb-rich precipitates at or near grain boundaries will act as crack arresters.
The Nb addition will promote a refined hierarchical microstructure.
The precipitate-containing microstructure will improve load distribution and reduce crack propagation.
Nb-rich precipitates will enhance grain-boundary cohesion and obstruct crack propagation, thereby increasing compressive strength and toughness.
The primary caloric matrix will remain intact after the Nb addition.
The Nb-rich phase will be inert with respect to the order-disorder or magnetostructural transitions responsible for the caloric response.
The Nb-modified material may reach or exceed approximately 250 MPa compressive strength.
The Nb-modified material will have greater crack resistance than the unchanged alloy.
The caloric temperature change of the Nb-modified material will remain within 10% of that of the unchanged alloy.
Epoxy- or In-based prior composite approaches achieved either strength up to approximately 218 MPa or improved heat transport, but not both simultaneously.
The intervention should remain effective under the same magnetic-field, pressure-field, and temperature regimes used for caloric operation.
Keeping the Nb content near 5 vol% and preventing precipitate percolation or coarsening is necessary to preserve performance.
Excessive refractory-element addition or precipitate growth can degrade compressive performance.
Excessive Nb addition may overly stiffen the alloy or alter its caloric mechanism.
Adding Nb preserves the rare-earth-free character of the stated alloy.

contradictions.description: The predicted-outcome field characterizes the unchanged alloy as showing compressive strengths of 152–218 MPa, whereas the baseline attributes values up to about 218 MPa to epoxy-containing composite approaches rather than to the unmodified alloy.
